title: Task 21e AI Provider Model Registry + Composer Dechrome

preparation.humanReviewSignal: User says the AI dialog is still too ugly and provider configuration allowing only one model is unreasonable; one provider account should support multiple selectable models.
preparation.architectureFinding: Jixia currently conflates provider credential/base URL/account configuration with model selection. AIProviderConfig has a single scalar model field across shared DTOs, API validation/service/repository, Prisma, settings UI, and chat composer selection.
preparation.visualMaturityScore: After Task21d, context semantics are correct but model/provider UX remains about 4/10 in data model/settings and about 6/10 in composer visual maturity because the composer selector is a providerConfig selector mislabeled as model.
externalDesignReferences: LobeChat provider/model switch and provider model settings patterns
Open WebUI model selector and admin model visibility patterns
Dify provider card nested model list and selector patterns
AnythingLLM provider-organized discovered model dropdown patterns
Chatbot UI provider-grouped lightweight model selector patterns
bindingDecisions: Split provider account/credential configuration from model profile selection.
One provider credential/base URL may own multiple model profiles without duplicating provider keys.
Existing AIProviderConfig.model data must migrate or backfill into a default model profile for backward compatibility.
Composer must select a model profile or equivalent server-resolved provider+model reference, not a provider config pretending to be a model.
Provider keys remain server-owned; browser must never receive raw/encrypted keys or call upstream providers directly.
Usage aggregation by provider+model remains valid after model-profile resolution.
Continue dechroming default chat surfaces: model choice should be a compact first-class chip/popover, not a visible provider status wall.
Use existing React/Mantine/CSS/Prisma/shared DTO patterns; do not add heavy UI frameworks or copy mature OSS stacks wholesale.
preparation.firstImplementationPriority: Introduce the provider/model registry contract and migration path first, then update settings and composer UX around model-profile selection while preserving existing AI run semantics.

noSuccessWithout: A provider/account can have multiple selectable model profiles without duplicating its provider key.
Existing single-model provider configs are migrated/backfilled into a default model profile.
Settings UI separates provider credential/base URL status from nested model profile management.
Composer selects a model profile or server-resolved provider+model reference and labels it honestly as a model selection.
Chat create/stream/run paths resolve provider credentials server-side and execute the selected model id.
Browser never receives raw/encrypted provider keys and never calls upstream AI providers directly.
Tests prove switching between two models under one provider changes the model sent to the provider path.
Document copilot context toggle/no-writeback guarantees from Task21d remain intact.
Manual/browser review records provider settings, composer picker, standalone chat, document copilot, and provider-key secrecy observations.
forbiddenCompletionClaims: Renaming providerConfigId to model is enough without splitting the data model.
Duplicating provider configs per model is acceptable mature UX.
The browser may store or inspect provider keys to support model switching.
A settings form with one free-text model field still satisfies multi-model provider support.
Model discovery/plugin marketplace is required for the first implementation.
Visual polish may add Tailwind, Framer Motion, Lucide, or upstream UI stacks just for aesthetics.
Task21e may regress document context off semantics or AI no-writeback behavior.
